cases.name: eval-prints-value
cases.doc: CLI parity: 'eval -e EXPR' prints the value of EXPR to stdout

cases.name: version-expr-42.2
cases.doc: CLI parity: (version) returns the runtime kernel version, ShenOSKernel 42.2 (set in init.kl), uniformly on every port (incl. shen-lua, which has no --version flag). Eval print is unquoted, so shen-c's 42.2 matches. Was version-expr-42 (Tarver S42.0) until every port moved to the community 42.2 kernel (pyrex41/bifrost#26).

cases.name: version-banner-contains
cases.doc: CLI parity: the --version banner contains the runtime kernel version 42.2. The standard launcher banner (extension-launcher.kl) leads with it, e.g. `42.2 (port ("Julia" "shen-julia") implementation (...))`. shen-lua has no --version flag, so Bifrost falls back to eval of (version). KNOWN PORT GAP: experimental shen-c prints a port-local `Shen-C 0.2.3` banner and FAILS here (it already did on Tarver S42.0); `bifrost impls --versions` falls back to eval of (version) for it.

cases.name: stdin-eof-clean-exit
cases.doc: DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENT OVER CANONICAL (not a spec conformance): starting the REPL and closing stdin (EOF) exits cleanly on every maintained impl. Canonical Shen LOOPS FOREVER here — the kernel shen.loop catches the reader's EOF error, prints it, and recurses (e.g. official shen-cl emits ~26MB of 'NIL is not of type CHARACTER' in 8s). All ports here detect EOF at the input layer and exit 0; this case guards that they keep doing so. (Earlier this passed spuriously for shen-cl because its repl adapter used a bare -q, which shen-cl rejects as an invalid arg and exits before the REPL even starts — now fixed to bare {bin}.) UPSTREAM shen-scheme 0.50 (tizoc release, the 42.2 reference) keeps the canonical loop and FAILS here by design (~5 MB/s of EOF errors until the timeout; Bifrost caps captured output at 8 MB). The pyrex41 shen-scheme fork reapplies its EOF exit on top of 0.50 (pyrex41/shen-scheme#9, `make test-repl-eof`).
